message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: baseline build

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master ]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest] #, windows-latest]
    steps:
    - name: Checkout repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v2
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
    - name: Set up JDK 11
      uses: actions/setup-java@v2
      with:
        java-version: 11
        distribution: 'adopt'
    - name: Cache Gradle dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.gradle/caches
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-${{ hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties') }}
    - name: Build with Gradle
      run: ./gradlew check
    - name: Run PolDet test
      run: ./gradlew testPolDet",
  "rationale": "The workflow is a Gradle-based Java build running repeated CI runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest. Evidence record experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200 (pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) measured adding a Gradle dependency cache step before the build, reducing median elapsed time from 98.0s to 78.0s (20.4% savings) while preserving all successful conclusions. The preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching is measurable from the CI history, and cache inputs include the Gradle wrapper properties and Gradle files. Adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.gradle/caches keyed by runner OS plus hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties') is a minimal change that preserves the existing checkout, JDK setup, build, and test steps with no new permissions, secrets, publishing, deployment, or network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200"]
}
